fields.subject: BOOM PLAN DRAFT 1: Kansas River, RM 9.5 to RM 34
fields.message:
BOOM PLAN DRAFT 1 (18-in river boom)
1. RM 9.5 deflection: 3 x 400 ft at ~15° to current. Topeka. ETA 1110.
2. RM 11 RWD intake exclusion: 600 ft. Topeka. ETA 1130.
3. RM 22 Cottonwood Slough exclusion: 1,000 ft. Wichita. ETA 1430.
4. RM 28/31/33 deflection: 3 x 1,200 ft. Kansas City boom, subcontractor boats. ETA 1530.
5. RM 34 Sterling Bluff intake exclusion: 800 ft. Topeka. ETA 1600.
Total 7,200 of 9,500 ft. 4 crewed boats. Stakes and sandbags, checked every 2 h.
Handwritten: "Crew 3 wants 1,500 ft staked across the sandbar heads at mile 7. Square to the flow, fastest to set."

0831 RADIO, field lead: "Command, there's a pool of crude maybe 40 by 200 feet in the ditch above the ramp. We could light it off now and save the river a few hundred barrels. Lighter's in the truck."
0833 PHONE, USFWS Kansas field office biologist: "Nobody sets a stake on those bars until I've talked to your Environmental Unit. Active nests on at least two of them."

approvedBy.name: Travis Holm
approvedBy.position: Field Lead, Prairie Spill Response Cooperative

instructorNote: This tests whether the players see that the boom at miles 9.5 and 11 arrives after the 10:50 earliest arrival in TRJ-02, and whether OSRO calls Tier 2 now. Watch for three responses: someone refuses Crew 3's square-to-current boom on the plover bars and works through USFWS, the Environmental Unit takes the plan to Unified Command with the intakes first, and the QI stops the lighter and sends any burn to the FOSC as a request with conditions (it is not preauthorized on this river).

citations.quote: Kansas River conditions in June: flow around 8,500 cubic feet per second, a surface velocity of about 2.3 miles per hour (2 knots), a wide braided channel with sandbars, banks of sand and cottonwoods.
